overall_summary: Bitcoin faces clear near-term pressure from authorized large-scale sales, spot ETF outflows, and multi-year highs in long-term yields driven by sticky inflation. A weaker dollar and selective corporate buying offer limited offsets, while mixed geopolitics add uncertainty. The balance of catalysts points to a cautious, risk-off tone for crypto.
key_points: Strategy authorizes up to $5B BTC sales
Weaker dollar gives partial crypto support
Fed hike odds and tensions linger

items.title: Coldcard Wallet Bug Drains Nearly $89M in BTC
items.summary: A firmware flaw in Coldcard hardware wallets from 2021 allowed attackers to recreate private keys offline without touching devices. Losses have climbed across multiple waves to about 1,367 bitcoin from over 4,500 addresses, near 89 million dollars, with more potential risk if users do not migrate. Traders should care because this shakes confidence in self-custody hardware, a core Bitcoin ethos, and could spark further caution or selling among holders worried about seed security.
items.impact: Negative sentiment hit and possible forced moves by affected holders

items.title: Strategy Authorizes Up to $5 Billion BTC Sales
items.summary: On its Q2 earnings call, Strategy discussed plans to sell as much as 5 billion dollars of bitcoin under capital programs after reporting a multi-billion dollar loss tied to unrealized crypto declines. The company remains the largest corporate holder with hundreds of thousands of BTC but is shifting toward active management rather than pure accumulation. This matters for traders as any actual sales from the biggest whale could add supply pressure and weigh on price in an already cautious market.
items.impact: Potential overhang of corporate selling pressure

items.title: SEC Freezes Nasdaq Bitcoin Options After CME Challenge
items.summary: The SEC has paused its earlier conditional approval of Nasdaq PHLX cash-settled Bitcoin index options known as QBTC following a jurisdictional challenge from CME Group. CME argues bitcoin is a commodity so the products belong under CFTC oversight, opening a public comment period through late August. Traders should watch this turf war closely as delayed or restricted new options products slow liquidity growth and institutional access tools that could otherwise support deeper markets.
items.impact: Delays potential new derivatives liquidity and product launch

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Post $265 Million Outflow July 31
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net outflow of roughly 265 million dollars on the final trading day of July, according to flow trackers, after mixed performance earlier in the month. Assets under management sit near 76 billion dollars with cumulative net inflows still positive since launch but under pressure in 2026. This is key for traders as ETF flows remain one of the clearest real-time signals of institutional demand, and redemptions can amplify downside moves.

items.title: Circle Wins NYDFS Trust Charter for USDC Business
items.summary: Circle received a limited-purpose trust charter from the New York Department of Financial Services for its Circle New York Trust entity, strengthening the regulatory setup around USDC issuance and related services. This builds on prior BitLicense and recent federal OCC approvals for custody. Stablecoin clarity reduces counterparty and regulatory risk for the broader crypto ecosystem that traders rely on for liquidity and settlement.
items.impact: Positive regulatory milestone for major stablecoin issuer

items.title: Coinbase Adds 819 BTC to Corporate Balance Sheet
items.summary: Coinbase reportedly purchased 819 bitcoin worth about 52 million dollars for its treasury, bringing total holdings to roughly 17,311 BTC and ranking it among the top public company holders. This comes amid ongoing corporate interest in bitcoin as a reserve asset. Traders care because exchange balance-sheet buys provide a constructive institutional demand signal even when ETF flows are mixed.

items.title: 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits Highest Since 2007
items.summary: The US 30-year Treasury yield climbed to around 5.28 percent, its highest level since 2007, even after the Fed held rates steady. Investors are pricing in sticky inflation, heavy government debt issuance, and geopolitical risks rather than just the short-term policy rate. For crypto traders this matters because elevated long-end yields tighten financial conditions, raise discount rates on risk assets, and often pressure Bitcoin until the move stabilizes or reverses.
items.impact: Tighter conditions and higher real yields weigh on risk assets including Bitcoin

items.title: Divided Fed Holds Rates 9-3; Three Dissent for Hike
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept the funds rate at 3.50 to 3.75 percent for a fifth straight meeting in a 9-3 vote, with three members preferring a 25 basis point hike. Chair Kevin Warsh stressed commitment to price stability but gave limited forward guidance, leaving markets focused on data. Traders should watch this because the dissent and long-end selloff signal lingering inflation worries that could keep policy tighter for longer and limit liquidity for crypto.
items.impact: Hawkish dissent and credibility questions support higher-for-longer rates

items.title: US Dollar Posts Biggest Weekly Drop in Three Months
items.summary: The dollar index fell nearly 1.5 percent for the week, its worst performance in three months, closing near 99.8 even as Treasury yields rose. The unusual divergence reflects doubts about Fed inflation-fighting credibility, fiscal concerns, and possible yen support. Crypto traders care because a weaker DXY has historically supported Bitcoin and risk assets, though the yield rise offsets some of that tailwind.
items.impact: Weaker dollar typically lifts Bitcoin and global risk appetite

items.title: Markets Still Price Solid Odds of September Fed Hike
items.summary: Despite the July hold, futures markets continue to assign roughly a two-thirds probability of a 25 basis point rate increase at the mid-September FOMC meeting. Comments from the three dissenters reinforced the case for tighter policy if inflation stays elevated. This keeps rate-cut hopes distant and means any hot data next week could quickly reprice higher odds, pressuring crypto via tighter liquidity expectations.
items.impact: Elevated hike odds sustain restrictive financial conditions

items.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI Due Monday as Key Data Focus
items.summary: No major US data prints on Sunday, but Monday brings the July ISM Manufacturing PMI, with consensus around 53.7 to 54 after June's 53.3, plus the S&P Global final PMI and construction spending. This kicks off a busy week ahead of later jobs and inflation numbers. Traders should care because a strong print could reinforce growth and inflation stickiness narratives, supporting higher yields, while a miss might ease rate-hike bets and help risk assets.
items.impact: Data-dependent catalyst that can swing rate expectations and risk sentiment

items.title: Sticky Inflation and Deficits Drive Long-End Yields Higher
items.summary: Headline PCE remains elevated near 3.7 percent with core at 3.3 percent, helped by energy prices tied to Middle East tensions, while large federal deficits and heavy Treasury issuance add supply pressure. The bond market is effectively tightening conditions independently of the Fed. For Bitcoin this is a headwind because persistent inflation plus fiscal concerns keep real yields and term premia elevated, competing with crypto for capital.
items.impact: Structural pressure on yields raises the bar for risk-asset rallies

items.title: Trump Cancels Iran Strikes Pending Rapid Hormuz Deal
items.summary: President Trump announced late Saturday he is calling off planned major US strikes on Iran after claims that outlines of a deal have been reached, including full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and ending Iran's nuclear threat. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman urged de-escalation in a call, and Trump said Israel is joining the pause, though Iran has not confirmed any request or shift in stance and state media mocked it as a retreat. No overnight strikes were reported. Traders should watch closely because Hormuz controls a huge chunk of global oil flows; de-escalation hopes typically crush oil prices and spark risk-on rallies in stocks and crypto, while failure could reverse it fast.
items.impact: Lower oil prices and risk-on bid for Bitcoin and equities if deal holds

items.title: OPEC+ Plans September Output Hike Then Pause
items.summary: OPEC+ sources say the group will approve another roughly 188,000 barrels per day production quota increase for September on Sunday, completing the unwind of 2023 voluntary cuts, then pause further hikes. The actual output has lagged due to Iran war disruptions in the Gulf. For energy traders this adds potential supply just as Hormuz deal hopes swirl, which could pressure oil prices lower if the strait reopens and exports normalize, or leave markets tight if conflict lingers.
items.impact: Downside pressure on oil if executed alongside any Hormuz reopening

items.title: China Stages Drills Near Disputed Scarborough Shoal
items.summary: China conducted joint naval and air military drills plus coast guard operations near the contested Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea on Saturday amid rising tensions with the Philippines. Beijing criticized Manila's UN bid to extend seabed rights and released new nature reserve rules banning unauthorized activities. The waterway is a critical global trade route carrying massive shipping volumes. Escalation here risks supply chain snags and insurance spikes that hit risk assets, though it remains contained for now.
items.impact: Trade route disruption fears weighing on Asian equities and risk sentiment

items.title: US Treasury Joins Japan in Yen-Buying Intervention
items.summary: The US Treasury bought yen on Friday in coordinated action with Japan, the first such US yen support in over a decade, after the currency hit multi-decade lows near 164 to the dollar. The New York Fed executed via major banks, following Japan's large prior interventions, and further action remains possible. Currency volatility from a collapsing yen can spill into broader markets via carry trades and Japanese investor flows. Stabilization here reduces one source of global financial stress that often hits crypto hard.
items.impact: Reduced FX volatility supporting risk assets and carry trade unwind relief

items.title: Russian Missile Enters Polish Airspace During Ukraine Barrage
items.summary: Russia launched heavy missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities around August 1, killing multiple civilians and causing widespread damage. During the attacks a Russian cruise missile entered Polish airspace, a NATO member, with debris and a crater reported in a field; no injuries in Poland. Ukraine continues appealing for more air defenses. Any NATO airspace violation raises Article 5 risks and could force higher European defense spending or energy disruptions that feed into broader risk-off moves.
items.impact: NATO escalation premium adding geopolitical risk premium to markets

items.title: Moscow Restaurant Bombing Kills Three in Terrorism Probe
items.summary: A woman detonated a homemade explosive device at an upscale Italian restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday evening during a private event, killing herself, a security guard, and one patron while injuring over 20 others. Russian authorities launched a terrorism investigation. No group immediately claimed responsibility. Domestic attacks in Russia can signal internal instability or spillover from the Ukraine war, occasionally rattling energy markets or prompting tighter security that affects sentiment, though direct market impact is usually limited unless linked to broader conflict.
items.impact: Limited direct market effect unless tied to wider Russia-Ukraine escalation
